questions.prompt: What does a Redis Hash store under a single key?

options.text: An ordered list of elements
A set of field-value pairs (a small dictionary)
A sorted collection ranked by score
A single string value only

questions.explanation: A Hash maps field names to values under one key, which makes it a natural fit for modeling an object like a user or product.

The total number of fields in the hash
The number of NEW fields added (existing ones are updated but not counted)
The value that was overwritten

questions.explanation: HSET returns how many fields were newly created; updates to existing fields still happen but don't add to that count.

questions.prompt: Which are genuine advantages of one hash over many separate string keys for an object? Select all that apply.

options.text: You can delete the whole object with a single DEL
Small hashes use less memory via a compact listpack encoding
You can fetch the whole object with one HGETALL
Every field automatically gets its own independent TTL by default

questions.explanation: Hashes give one-key management, memory savings, and one-shot fetch. Per-field TTLs are NOT the default — they require Redis 7.4+; normally a TTL applies to the whole key.

questions.prompt: Why can HGETALL be risky on a very large hash?

options.text: It deletes fields as it reads them
It returns every field-value pair in one O(N) blocking command
It only works on hashes with fewer than 10 fields
It requires the hash to be sorted first

questions.explanation: HGETALL doesn't paginate — it returns all fields at once, which is O(N) and can block the server on a huge hash. Use HSCAN to iterate instead.

questions.prompt: The command that atomically adds an integer to a numeric field of a hash is ______. (one word)
questions.explanation: HINCRBY adds an integer to a hash field atomically (HINCRBYFLOAT does the same for floating-point amounts).

questions.prompt: Which statement about HMSET is correct?

options.text: It is the only way to set multiple fields
It is deprecated; HSET now accepts multiple field-value pairs
It sets a field only if it does not exist
It sets a TTL on each field

questions.explanation: HMSET is deprecated. Modern HSET accepts multiple field-value pairs, so HSET covers both single and multi-field writes.
